items.headline: Apple Gets Win in User Data Court Case Against UK Government
items.excerpt: A UK court has rejected the British government’s attempt to keep secret an order it sent to Apple Inc. seeking access to the encrypted data of customers.

items.headline: Anthropic Shares Soar Above IPO Price, Then Fall
items.excerpt: Anthropic PBC shares traded 17% above their IPO price after the company's $107.3 billion debut, but shares dropped later in the session. Bloomberg's Ryan Gould and Bailey Lipschultz report on the first volatile day of trading on the Nasdaq. (Source: Bloomberg)

items.headline: Uber Tests Rides for 10- to 12-Year-Olds in Three US Cities
items.excerpt: Uber Technologies Inc. said parents of kids who are 10 to 12 years old can order rides on their behalf as part of a limited testing program in the US.

items.headline: Google’s Gemini Can Now Control Mac Devices on Users’ Behalf
items.excerpt: Google’s Gemini can now take control of Mac computers to complete tasks for users, matching a feature already offered by other popular AI assistants and raising the pressure on Apple Inc. to make Siri more capable.

items.headline: Nscale’s ByteDance Deal Faces Scrutiny Under US Chip Curbs
items.excerpt: Nscale Plc’s agreement to sell artificial intelligence computing capacity to ByteDance Ltd. will come under greater regulatory scrutiny after the US moved to crack down on China’s access to American technology overseas.

items.headline: Anthropic Makes Trading Debut With Record Breaking IPO
items.excerpt: Anthropic shares soared above their opening price after the AI company's record breaking $107.3 billion IPO, becoming the first pure-play AI lab to go public. items.headline: Assassin’s Creed Owner Sees 26% Drop in Holiday Quarter Bookings
items.excerpt: Ubisoft Entertainment SA forecast a 26% drop in holiday period bookings as the Assassin’s Creed maker goes up against the new Grand Theft Auto VI and what the French company called a particularly “crowded” season.

items.headline: Anthropic Makes History on Wall Street
items.excerpt: Get a jump start on the US trading day with Dani Burger on "Bloomberg Open Interest." Anthropic makes history on Wall Street. items.headline: Anthropic Begins Trading on Nasdaq at $111.50
items.excerpt: Anthropic shares open on the Nasdaq and soar 21% above their IPO price. Evan Schlossman, vice president of investor relations at Neostellar Capital Corp., says this is an exciting day. He speaks to Bloomberg's Scarlet Fu. (Source: Bloomberg)

items.excerpt: Ahead of Anthropic shares listing on the Nasdaq, Altimeter’s Pauline Yang discusses why the firm added to its Anthropic position in the offering, how improving compute economics transformed its investment thesis, and why she sees room for both Anthropic and OpenAI to become multi-trillion-dollar

items.excerpt: In this episode of Power On, Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman is joined by technology journalist and reviewer Joanna Stern of The New Things and NBC News for a critical look at Apple’s software leadership and its struggles to compete in artificial intelligence. items.excerpt: Anthropic shares opened at $111.50, roughly 34% above their $83 IPO price, after the company completed the biggest IPO in history. items.headline: Apple’s iPhone Camera and Photos Software Chief Jon McCormack Leaves Company
items.excerpt: Apple Inc.’s head of camera and photo software has left, marking a rare shake-up in the leadership behind one of the iPhone’s most important features.

items.headline: Bitcoin Pares Gain as Anthropic Fails to Sustain Risk Appetite
items.excerpt: Bitcoin pared gains after Anthropic PBC’s market debut failed to sustain enthusiasm for the artificial-intelligence trade, weighing on most riskier assets.

items.headline: Google Workers Urge Bosses to Give Schools Search Without AI
items.excerpt: Hundreds of Google employees are urging the tech giant to curb its aggressive approach to rolling out artificial intelligence in K-12 schools.

items.headline: Electronics Industry Faces Global Circuit Board Shortage
items.excerpt: The worldwide economy is staring down a gaping shortage of a foundational component found in nearly every consumer product that contains electronics, according to a new advisory from the Global Electronics Association.

items.headline: Anthropic IPO Provides Cash to Continue R&D Spending, CFO Says
items.excerpt: Anthropic PBC’s public market debut will allow the company to keep investing to stay ahead on AI, as the Claude chatbot maker devotes about 75% of its computing capacity to research and development, Anthropic Chief Financial Officer Krishna Rao said Thursday.

items.headline: AI Financing Shifts From Hyperscalers to Chips: Berro
items.excerpt: Kelsey Berro, fixed income portfolio manager at JPMorgan Asset Management, says record demand has absorbed a surge in hyperscaler debt, but the next test for AI financing will come from chips. “2027, it’s gonna be about the chip financing,” Berro says on “Bloomberg Surveillance.” (Source: Bloomberg)

items.headline: European Stocks Decline in Longest Losing Streak Since August
items.excerpt: European stocks fell for a fourth straight day, weighed down by defensive sectors, as investors awaited the start of trading in Anthropic PBC’s shares after a blockbuster initial public offering.

items.headline: Zino: Anthropic is Most Important IPO That I've Seen
